title: Phoenix
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Osamu Tezuka's unfinished 'life's work': twelve self-contained stories ranging from third-century Japan to the far future, linked by the Phoenix, an immortal firebird whose blood is said to grant eternal life. Rulers, soldiers, artists and scientists chase or meet her across eras, and characters recur through reincarnation as their deeds in one life shape suffering in another (Wikipedia; ANN House of 1000 Manga; AniList).
life_message: Life is precious because it passes; chasing immortality and power brings suffering, while compassion breaks the cycle of karma.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Humanity and all life, not clan, is the frame.

folkways.japan: Buddhist karma, Shinto myth from the Kojiki era and postwar Japanese pacifism inform Tezuka's epic, described here as context.

delivery.evidence: ANN says ideas come through adventure and romance, 'sometimes profoundly, sometimes goofily'; Time called it enlightening (Wikipedia).

personified.ideology: Bitter bandit transformed by karma and art

delivery.note: Each story embodies the craving for immortality or power in characters who are given human motives before their fall.

winners_losers: No one owns the Phoenix; tyrants and immortality-seekers fall, while those who accept mortality and show compassion are favored. The Buddhist view of karma receives sympathy.
